problem: If $g(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+5)-1,$ find ${({g}^{-1})}^{′}(x)$ as a function of ${g}^{-1}(x).$

feedback.worked_solution:
**Step 1:** First, we write the inverse function implicitly. The given function is $y={sin}^{3}⁡({x}^{2}),$ and to write the inverse function implicitly, we swap $x$ and $y$ as follows:

$$
x={sin}^{3}⁡({y}^{2})
$$

Note that in the equation above, we have $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

**Step 2:** Next, we differentiate. The overall goal is to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ but the equation is already solved for $x,$ so we compute $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}$ and then take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({sin}^{3}⁡({y}^{2})) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =3{sin}^{2}⁡({y}^{2})\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})\cdot 2y \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =6y{sin}^{2}⁡({y}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{6y{sin}^{2}⁡({y}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡({y}^{2})\operatorname{sec}⁡({y}^{2})}{6y}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3:** Lastly, we write the result in terms of ${f}^{-1}(x).$ Since $y={f}^{-1}(x),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{f}^{-1}(x)] & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡({[{f}^{-1}(x)]}^{2})\operatorname{sec}⁡({[{f}^{-1}(x)]}^{2})}{6{f}^{-1}(x)} \\ {({f}^{-1})}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡({[{f}^{-1}(x)]}^{2})\operatorname{sec}⁡({[{f}^{-1}(x)]}^{2})}{6{f}^{-1}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$
